name: ERROR.TYPE
description: ERROR.TYPE returns a number identifying which error value is in the supplied cell: 1 for #NULL!, 2 for #DIV/0!, 3 for #VALUE!, 4 for #REF!, 5 for #NAME?, 6 for #NUM!, and 7 for #N/A.
tldr: Returns a number code for an error type.

parameters.name: error_val
parameters.description: A reference to a cell (or a value) that contains an Excel error.

basicExample.explanation: A1 contains #DIV/0!, which maps to code 2.

advancedExamples.title: Safe lookup with a guard
advancedExamples.scenario: Return the code only when an error exists.
advancedExamples.description: Avoid ERROR.TYPE's own #N/A on good values
advancedExamples.explanation: When A1 is fine, ISERROR is FALSE so the formula returns "no error" instead of triggering #N/A.

howItWorks: ERROR.TYPE returns a numeric code for the error in error_val: 1=#NULL!, 2=#DIV/0!, 3=#VALUE!, 4=#REF!, 5=#NAME?, 6=#NUM!, 7=#N/A. If error_val is not an error, ERROR.TYPE itself returns #N/A. Pair it with ISERROR or IFERROR before calling.

howToSteps.name: Confirm an error exists
howToSteps.text: Use ISERROR on the cell first.

howToSteps.name: Map the code
howToSteps.text: Use CHOOSE or a lookup to turn the number into an error name.

limitations: Returns #N/A when given a non-error value.
Works only on an actual error value, not on a text label like "#DIV/0!".
Only returns a code; you must map it to a name yourself.

commonErrors.cause: The argument is not an error value.
commonErrors.fix: Guard with ISERROR or IFERROR before calling it.

commonErrors.cause: The code numbers are easy to mix up.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ERROR.TYPE works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and codes.

faq.question: What if there is no error?
faq.answer: ERROR.TYPE returns #N/A, so always guard it.
